Subject: Post-demo: subprocessor list + SOC 2 / vendor questionnaire

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Summary: showed Redwood inference platform, routing/policy controls, and our Dedicated offering that lets you isolate workloads.
- Action items: we agreed to share our subprocessor list and SOC 2 report, and to kick off your vendor security questionnaire.

I attached an initial subprocessor list (summary PDF) — this covers cloud infra providers, logging/monitoring vendors, and a short description of dataflows and retention boundaries. Notes on compliance:
- SOC 2: Redwood completed a Type II in 2026; I’ll share the report link in my next email (and happy to provide redacted sections if your procurement team needs them).
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support customer-controlled data deletion and can scope private deployments for PHI. If HIPAA is in scope we typically recommend the Private deployment + dedicated KMS.

Next steps from me:
1) Share SOC 2 link and updated subprocessor list (attaching v1).
2) Send over an editable questionnaire link so your security team can complete it.

Can you confirm who on your side should receive the SOC 2 report (PDF link) vs. who should complete the vendor questionnaire?

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. Our security team (cc'd: Bob Lee, Security Ops) will need the full SOC 2 Type II report and a detailed subprocessor list showing which processors see customer data vs. aggregated/telemetry. A few clarifying Qs:

- Is the subprocessor list versioned and do you provide a notification window for changes?
- Do you have any subprocessors that perform model training on customer data or could access raw customer prompts?
- In terms of data residency, can we restrict logs to our AWS region for Dedicated/Private deployments?

On our side: Bob will own the vendor questionnaire. Please send the Doc/Link for completion. For the SOC 2 report, we prefer a secure drive link (we will treat it as confidential).

Thanks,
Alicia

Subject: Re: Post-demo: subprocessor list + SOC 2 / vendor questionnaire

Hi Alicia / Bob —

Thanks for the quick reply — answers below and next steps:

- Versioning/notifications: yes, subprocessor_list_v1.pdf is the current snapshot. We provide 30 days' notice for material subprocessor changes for customers on Dedicated and Private contracts; hosted API customers receive in-product notifications + email.
- Training/access to prompts: Redwood does not use customer prompts for model training. For Hosted customers, model telemetry is aggregated and access-controlled; for Private/Dedicated we can disable telemetry collection by agreement.
- Data residency: For Private/Dedicated, logs and persistent storage can be provisioned in your AWS region (we'll include region-scoped S3 buckets and KMS keys).

Attached: subprocessor_list_v1.pdf (summary). I’m also sharing our SOC 2 Type II report via a secure Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=SOC2-REPORT-2026 (let me know if you need an NDA/redacted sections).

Vendor questionnaire: please use this secure questionnaire link so we capture structured answers — https://forms.qualtrics.com/s/AcmeVendorQuestionnaire (Bob, you can save a copy/export when complete).

If you want, Rishi (cc'd) can join a short call to walk through the infra boundaries and KMS options. Proposed times: Wed 5/14 10am PT or Thu 5/15 11am PT.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks all — quick internal notes:

- Confirmed: SOC 2 Type II 2026 available; share link but be prepared to provide redacted report for procurement.
- Subprocessors: current list includes AWS (EC2, S3), GCP (for some regions), Datadog, Sentry (monitoring), Segment (telemetry) and HashiCorp Vault (secrets). None have access to raw prompts for training.
- Notify legal about potential DPA clauses Acme will require (data residency + deletion windows). I will draft recommended language for Dedicated/Private customers and circulate to Marissa + Rishi by EOD tomorrow.

Marissa — please confirm which attachment version we want to keep in the vendor portal (I suggest v1 for now; we'll bump to v1.1 when legal finalizes the DPA language).

Neha Kapoor
